title: Split pea and parsnip stew with purple sprouting broccoli

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain cupboard or garden staple: split peas, tinned tomatoes, stock, spices and fresh vegetables.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item, including the purple sprouting broccoli, which is on sale in January.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, a board and one large lidded pan, and the technique is simple simmering and steaming.

works.reason: 250g split peas in 1.2 litres of stock with parsnips and 300g broccoli makes a sensible stew for four, and 50 minutes' simmering with a water top-up should soften the peas.

honest_times.reason: Chopping two onions and three parsnips, crushing garlic and trimming the broccoli fits 20 minutes, and the steps add up to about 63 minutes against the 60 printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the lemon, cumin and turmeric, is used, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming split pea stew suits mid-January, and 300g of purple sprouting broccoli steamed on top is a real part of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pulses, root vegetables and greens make a filling, wholesome family dinner.
